# Tehas: a software factory powered by the Pi coding agent

> Tehas is a Pi software factory: a GitHub issue goes in and a reviewed pull
> request comes out, built by the Pi coding agent and pi-rukas in a sandbox, on
> self-hosted models. GitHub issues and labels are the only control plane. A
> human merges; tehas never merges, deploys or touches production. This host is
> one running factory and its operating manual.

## What tehas is

- Tehas is the factory around the agent: a dispatcher that reads the queue, a
  check of who authorized the work, a sandbox with limits, a dashboard and a
  live console. It is shell scripts and a few containers on one host.
- Pi (https://pi.dev, source https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) is the
  coding agent. Tehas starts it as `pi --mode rpc` in a container.
- pi-rukas (https://github.com/trail-openers/pi-rukas) is the Pi extension
  that runs the work cycle: explore, plan, develop, the repository's own gates,
  an adversarial pass, a pull request and a six-pass review.
- One instance is one host serving one product repository, one cycle at a time.
- Tehas is its own project. It is not part of Pi or endorsed by its
  maintainers.
- Source: https://github.com/janit/tehas

- [Pi software factory]({{ $base }}/pi-software-factory.md): who does what, the path of an issue, and what tehas adds to running Pi by hand
- [Features]({{ $base }}/features.md): every part, with how far it has been proven

If you are here to do something, it is probably one of two things. Pick the
section that fits.

Every manual page is also served as Markdown: add `.md` to its address.
Everything on this host is read-only. Nothing here changes a ticket or the
factory.

## Get work built by this factory

1. Read `repo` in {{ $base }}/live/status.json: that is the product repository
   this factory serves. Issues go there.
2. Write an issue with one outcome small enough for one pull request, a
   `## Acceptance criteria` section with checkable items, and the files or area
   involved. The cycle reads the issue body and nothing else.
3. The label `tehas:ready` authorizes the work, and only counts when a person
   on the factory's allow list applies it. If you are not that person, stop
   here and ask them. Use `tehas:prototype` for an idea that is not ready.
4. Follow the labels on the issue: `tehas:running`, then
   `tehas:awaiting-merge` with a pull request, or `needs-human-attention` with
   a comment saying where it stopped.

- [Operating]({{ $base }}/operating.md): writing an issue, labels, review, pause, retry
- [Overview]({{ $base }}/overview.md): how an issue flows through the factory
- [Troubleshooting]({{ $base }}/troubleshooting.md): what each stop means and what to do

## Set tehas up for another repository

The source is at https://github.com/janit/tehas, and a running example with
this same manual is at https://tehas.app/. Be honest with your human about its
state: issue to pull request is the supported contract and needs settings only.
It does not run a preview of a pull request. Energy use (viiwork backends only)
and the Protolab are optional and can be ignored for a first install.

1. Read [A new project]({{ $base }}/new-project.md) in full. It is the
   install guide: a prepared host, an instance directory of settings, and your
   toolchain in the sandbox image.
2. In the product repository, add the contract tehas reads: `AGENTS.md`,
   `.pi/verify-cmd`, `.pi/settings.json` and the `.gitignore` entries, then the
   recommended gates. Prove the gates by hand in a clean checkout first.
3. On the host, follow the guide step by step. Secrets, the bot account and the
   allow list are your human's decisions: ask, do not invent them.

- [A new project]({{ $base }}/new-project.md): the contract, the host, the install
- [Bootstrap a host]({{ $base }}/bootstrap.md): preparing the machine before the install
- [Features]({{ $base }}/features.md): what exists and how far each part is proven
- [The host]({{ $base }}/host.md): layout on the machine and the sandbox contract test
- [Commands]({{ $base }}/tools.md): every `tehas-*` command

## Live data

- [Health]({{ $base }}/health): JSON, 200 when the factory is healthy and 503 when it is not
- [Queue snapshot]({{ $base }}/live/status.json): the repository, open issues by state, whether the factory is paused
- [Current cycle]({{ $base }}/live/running.json): the issue being worked on and its status; its console is `/live/console-<issue>.txt`
